service_boundary: Represents Eden AI's aggregation API across several model categories, not the upstream vendors it forwards to.
regional_controls: The operator is a French company and documents European data governance; upstream processing geography follows the selected provider.
retention_controls: The terms state customer data is not used to train models and that prompts and outputs are not stored by default, with limited billing metadata retained. The operator explicitly disclaims control over upstream providers' retention.
routing: Requests are directed to a selected vendor for a chosen capability, with fallback across vendors for the same task.
customization: The service focuses on aggregating existing vendor models across categories rather than customer fine-tuning.
strengths: Coverage extends past language models to document, speech, translation, and vision vendors through one contract and one request format.
The operator is a named French company with dated terms and a stated position on training and storage.
tradeoffs: Documented model and provider counts differ across the vendor's own pages.
Breadth across model categories means the effective data boundary varies by which vendor a request reaches.
Whether platform fees apply to customer-supplied provider keys is not documented.

response_integrity.note: No signature, attestation, or equivalent mechanism for verifying that a response arrived unaltered from the upstream model appears on the security page or in the LLM documentation.
response_integrity.scope: Eden AI security page, for the Eden AI API

upstream_disclosure.note: The provider data-policies page states: "When you call a model through Eden AI, your request is forwarded to the underlying provider, whose own policy governs what happens to it." It carries a per-provider table of training use, retention, and zero-data-retention availability.
upstream_disclosure.scope: Eden AI provider data-policies page, for the Eden AI API

credential_handling.note: The bring-your-own-key page states: "Eden AI lets you use your own provider API keys (OpenAI, Google, Anthropic, etc.) instead of going through Eden AI's billing." Neither it nor the security page says how those keys are stored or whether they are encrypted at rest.
credential_handling.scope: Eden AI bring-your-own-key page, for the Eden AI API

cache_isolation.note: The prompt-caching page states: "The cache belongs to the provider endpoint that handled the request. It is not shared between providers, regions, accounts, or unrelated models." The page does not define whether "accounts" means Eden AI customers or the upstream accounts Eden AI holds, which matters for traffic on Eden AI's own credentials.
cache_isolation.scope: Eden AI prompt-caching page, for the Eden AI API

vulnerability_disclosure.note: No security contact or disclosure policy appears on the security page, which offers only a general contact link.
vulnerability_disclosure.scope: Eden AI security page, for the Eden AI API

independent_audit.note: The security page states: "Eden AI is SOC 2 and ISO 27001 certified, demonstrating independently assessed security controls and a structured information security management system." No certificate, report, or auditor is linked.
independent_audit.scope: Eden AI security page, for the Eden AI API
